```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Run-checklist state, shared by the Protocol section's checkable steps below.
// Persisted to localStorage so it survives a reload; "Reset checklist" clears it.
mutable checkedSteps = (() => {
  try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("citraprep-checklist-v1") || "{}"); } catch (e) { return {}; }
})()

setStepChecked = (id, isChecked) => {
  const next = {...checkedSteps, [id]: isChecked};
  mutable checkedSteps = next;
  try { localStorage.setItem("citraprep-checklist-v1", JSON.stringify(next)); } catch (e) {}
}

resetChecklist = () => {
  mutable checkedSteps = {};
  try { localStorage.removeItem("citraprep-checklist-v1"); } catch (e) {}
}

// One checkable row. `content` is plain text (numbers already stand out as text).
// Built with plain DOM calls rather than an onchange=${...} attribute in an html``
// template — that pattern was silently failing to bind and leaking its own source
// text onto the page instead of rendering a working checkbox.
checkStep = (id, content) => {
  const input = document.createElement("input");
  input.type = "checkbox";
  input.style.cssText = "margin-top:3px;flex-shrink:0;";
  input.checked = !!checkedSteps[id];
  input.onchange = (e) => setStepChecked(id, e.target.checked);

  const span = document.createElement("span");
  span.style.cssText = `flex:1;${checkedSteps[id] ? "opacity:.55;text-decoration:line-through;" : ""}`;
  span.textContent = content;

  const label = document.createElement("label");
  label.style.cssText = "display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:flex-start;background:var(--bs-body-bg, #fff);border:1px solid var(--bs-border-color, #dee2e6);border-radius:8px;padding:8px 10px;margin-bottom:6px;cursor:pointer;";
  label.append(input, span);
  return label;
}

allStepIds = [
  "homog-a","homog-b","homog-c","homog-d","homog-e","homog-f","homog-g",
  "grad-a","grad-b","grad-c","grad-d","grad-e",
  "wash-1","wash-2","wash-3","wash-4","wash-5","wash-6"
]
checkedCount = allStepIds.filter(id => checkedSteps[id]).length
totalCount   = allStepIds.length
progressPct  = totalCount ? Math.round(checkedCount / totalCount * 100) : 0
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Overview
CitraPrep isolates intact nuclei from snap-frozen tissue for downstream single-nucleus work. Tissue is dounce-homogenized in a citrate-based homogenization buffer (CitraHB), then nuclei are purified on an iodixanol step gradient in an **ultracentrifuge** (18 min run, ~1 hr total with load/accel/no-brake coast, 10,000×g, **no brake**) and collected from the gradient interface. RNase inhibitors (RNasin Ribonuclease Inhibitor + Protector RNase Inhibitor) go into **every** buffer, including the final nuclei wash / resuspension buffer. Spermine, spermidine, and dithiothreitol (DTT) are deliberately left **out** of that buffer because they interfere with downstream cDNA synthesis.

For small, soft tissue that doesn't need a density gradient, see the **SeaPrep** protocol instead.

<!-- TODO: confirm source/citation for this protocol with JP -->
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Before starting
- Use **cell culture grade water** for every "water" call in this protocol (stock buffers and 1000X fresh solutions alike), not general lab ddH₂O.
- Make 1 M Tricine–Potassium Hydroxide (Tricine-KOH, pH 7.8) and 1 M Citric Acid stocks first; CitraHB and Diluent are both built from them.
- Prepare CitraHB, Diluent, and Detergent stock buffers **a day ahead**; good for 1 month at 4°C.
- Pre-chill the 7 mL glass dounce homogenizer on ice.
- Hand-dounce only: **no motorized homogenizer**, it shears nuclei and causes blebbing.
- Make 1 M Dithiothreitol (DTT), 0.15 M spermine, and 0.5 M spermidine (1000X stocks) **fresh** each time.
- Make CitraHB Complete (stock + protease inhibitor tablet) fresh; add spermine/spermidine/DTT to bring it to 1X.
- Make the nuclei wash / resuspension buffer while the gradient is running, with **no** spermine, spermidine, or DTT in this one.
- Set the ultracentrifuge to 4°C and confirm the rotor/tubes are rated for **no-brake** deceleration.
- Book more time than the spin itself. The 18 min is only the run; loading, vacuum draw-down, acceleration, and the unbraked coast to a stop routinely bring the whole ultracentrifuge step to **around an hour**.
:::

---

## Configure experiment

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof n_samples  = Inputs.number({label: "Number of samples", value: 1, min: 1, max: 24, step: 1})
viewof excess_pct = Inputs.number({label: "Extra overage on scaled solutions (%)", value: 0, min: 0, max: 30, step: 5})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Per-sample working volumes. CitraHB Complete is made in 10 mL increments
// (whole protease inhibitor tablets), so its total is always rounded UP to the
// next 10 mL — set the per-sample number here and the table below does the rest.
viewof chb_per_sample = Inputs.number({label: "CitraHB Complete per sample (mL) — two-round dounce uses ≈ 5", value: 10, min: 1, step: 1})
viewof wash_per_spin  = Inputs.number({label: "Nuclei wash / resuspension volume per spin (mL)", value: 10, min: 1, step: 1})
viewof n_wash_spins   = Inputs.number({label: "Number of nuclei wash spins", value: 1, min: 0, max: 5, step: 1})
viewof final_resus_uL = Inputs.number({label: "Final resuspension volume (µL)", value: 200, min: 50, step: 50})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// RNase inhibitor final AND stock concentrations, per inhibitor. RNasin and
// Protector don't always ship at the same strength (commonly 40 U/µL or
// 20 U/µL) — check your tubes. Set a final conc to 0 to leave that inhibitor out.
viewof rnasin_final = Inputs.number({label: "RNasin Ribonuclease Inhibitor final conc. (U/µL, each buffer)", value: 0.5, min: 0, step: 0.05})
viewof rnasin_stock = Inputs.number({label: "RNasin stock conc. (U/µL)", value: 40, min: 1, step: 1})
viewof protector_final   = Inputs.number({label: "Protector RNase Inhibitor final conc. (U/µL, each buffer)", value: 0.5, min: 0, step: 0.05})
viewof protector_stock   = Inputs.number({label: "Protector stock conc. (U/µL)", value: 40, min: 1, step: 1})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
scale = n_samples * (1 + excess_pct / 100)
fmt   = (x, d = 2) => x.toFixed(d)

// Stock volume needed to hit a final conc in total volume V (V and result share units).
rnasin_vol = (V) => rnasin_final * V / rnasin_stock
protector_vol   = (V) => protector_final   * V / protector_stock

md`**${n_samples} sample(s) · ${excess_pct}% overage · RNasin ${rnasin_final} U/µL (stock ${rnasin_stock}) · Protector ${protector_final} U/µL (stock ${protector_stock})**`
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Running low on inhibitor? There's flexibility here
The default 0.5 U/µL RNasin + 0.5 U/µL Protector split (1 U/µL total) is a precaution, not something backed by a side-by-side experiment — per Marissa. If you only have one of the two on hand, **1 U/µL of a single inhibitor is fine**: set one of the two final-conc toggles above to 0 and the other to 1. Short on total inhibitor too? **As low as 0.8 U/µL total is passable** in a pinch.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Ordering quantities
Per sample, keep roughly **1 mL RNasin** and **500 µL Protector** (RNase inhibitor) on hand. The line-item breakdown below is the granular per-buffer calculation; it will not sum to exactly this figure, since the ordering number is a rough estimate rather than a derived total.
:::

---

## Stock buffers

Make ~1 month's supply at once; store at 4°C. These do **not** scale with sample count; they're a standing stock, not a per-run master mix.

### 1 M stock reagents (make first)

CitraHB and Diluent both draw their Tricine-KOH and Citric Acid components from 1 M stocks. Pick a batch volume and the amounts scale automatically.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof stock_vol_mL = Inputs.number({label: "1M stock batch volume (mL)", value: 100, min: 10, step: 10})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
tricine_MW = 179.17
citric_MW  = 192.124

tricine_g = 1 * (stock_vol_mL / 1000) * tricine_MW
citric_g  = 1 * (stock_vol_mL / 1000) * citric_MW

Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Tricine (free acid)", "Amount": `${fmt(tricine_g)} g`, "Recipe": `Dissolve in ~80% of ${fmt(stock_vol_mL)} mL cell culture grade water; titrate to pH 7.8 with Potassium Hydroxide (KOH); bring to ${fmt(stock_vol_mL)} mL`},
  {Component: "Citric Acid",         "Amount": `${fmt(citric_g)} g`,  "Recipe": `Dissolve in cell culture grade water to ${fmt(stock_vol_mL)} mL`}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Why Tricine needs KOH and citric acid doesn't
Tricine-KOH is the free-acid form of Tricine titrated to pH 7.8 with Potassium Hydroxide (KOH); the "-KOH" in the name refers to this titration, not a separate reagent added at the bench. Citric Acid stock is used as-is; both CitraHB and Diluent get their acidic character partly from it, so no pH adjustment is needed here.
:::

**CitraHB**

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
sucrose_MW = 342.2965
kcl_MW     = 74.5513
mgcl2_MW   = 95.211

citrahb_need_mL = chb_vol + citrahb_40 + citrahb_30   // CitraHB Complete + both iodixanol dilutions — Detergent draws more on top, see note below
viewof citrahb_batch_mL = Inputs.number({label: "CitraHB batch volume (mL)", value: Math.max(30, Math.ceil(citrahb_need_mL / 10) * 10), min: 10, step: 10})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
citrahb_sucrose_g  = 0.25  * (citrahb_batch_mL / 1000) * sucrose_MW
citrahb_kcl_g      = 0.025 * (citrahb_batch_mL / 1000) * kcl_MW
citrahb_mgcl2_g    = 0.005 * (citrahb_batch_mL / 1000) * mgcl2_MW
citrahb_tricine_uL = 20 * citrahb_batch_mL
citrahb_citric_uL  = 10 * citrahb_batch_mL

md`**This run needs ≈ ${fmt(citrahb_need_mL)} mL** of CitraHB stock (CitraHB Complete + the 40%/30% iodixanol dilutions) — plus whatever your Detergent batch draws on top (320 µL/sample × ${n_samples} sample(s) ≈ ${fmt(n_samples * 0.32)} mL, pulled from this same stock).`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Sucrose",                      "Final conc.": "0.25 M", "Amount": `${fmt(citrahb_sucrose_g)} g`},
  {Component: "Potassium Chloride (KCl)",     "Final conc.": "25 mM",  "Amount": `${fmt(citrahb_kcl_g * 1000, 1)} mg`},
  {Component: "Magnesium Chloride (MgCl₂)",   "Final conc.": "5 mM",   "Amount": `${fmt(citrahb_mgcl2_g * 1000, 1)} mg`},
  {Component: "Tricine-KOH pH 7.8",           "Final conc.": "20 mM",  "Amount": `${fmt(citrahb_tricine_uL, 0)} µL of 1 M stock`},
  {Component: "Citric Acid",                  "Final conc.": "10 mM",  "Amount": `${fmt(citrahb_citric_uL, 0)} µL of 1 M stock`}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

Dissolve in cell culture grade water to the batch volume above.

```{ojs}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

**Detergent (1 mL)**

| Component | Amount |
|-----------|--------|
| IGEPAL CA-630 | 50 µL |
| CitraHB | 950 µL |

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Buffer storage
CitraHB, Diluent, and Detergent are stable at 4°C for up to 1 month. Scale any of these recipes linearly if you need a larger batch; the ratios above hold regardless of final volume.
:::

---

## Fresh working solutions (1000X stocks)

Make fresh each time; do not store.

| Component | Final stock | Recipe |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| 1 M Dithiothreitol (DTT) | 1000X | 0.15425 g in 1 mL cell culture grade water |
| 0.15 M spermine | 1000X | 0.03035 g in 1 mL cell culture grade water |
| 0.5 M spermidine | 1000X | 0.072625 g in 1 mL cell culture grade water |

Add spermine, spermidine, and Dithiothreitol (DTT) to all buffers below for a final 1X concentration, **except** the nuclei wash / resuspension buffer (see warning below).

Add RNase inhibitor to all buffers below at the final concentrations set in **Configure experiment** above. The defaults are 0.5 U/µL RNasin Ribonuclease Inhibitor (RNasin) and 0.5 U/µL Protector RNase Inhibitor (Protector), 1 U/µL total. RNasin and Protector don't always ship at the same stock strength (commonly 40 U/µL or 20 U/µL); check your tubes, set all four values up top, and every table below rescales. Both are referred to by their short names (RNasin, Protector) throughout the rest of this document.

---

## Working solutions: scaled to sample count

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Math audit: how every volume is calculated

**CitraHB Complete** — made in 10 mL increments because each aliquot takes one whole protease inhibitor tablet, so the total is rounded **up** to the next 10 mL:

$$V_{make} = \left\lceil \frac{v_{per\ sample} \times N_{samples} \times (1 + overage)}{10} \right\rceil \times 10 \qquad tablets = \frac{V_{make}}{10}$$

RNase inhibitors and the 1000X polyamine/DTT additives scale linearly with $V_{make}$.

**Nuclei wash / resuspension buffer** — one pool covers the wash spin(s) and the final resuspension:

$$V_{buffer} = \left( v_{wash} \times n_{spins} + \frac{V_{final\ \mu L}}{1000} \right) \times N_{samples} \times (1 + overage)$$

Default is one wash spin of 10 mL plus a 200 µL final resuspension ≈ 10 mL/sample. Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) is 1% w/v of $V_{buffer}$; RNasin and Protector use $V_{stock} = (C_{final}/C_{stock}) \times V_{buffer}$, each with its own stock strength. No spermine, spermidine, or DTT; these interfere with downstream cDNA synthesis.

**Iodixanol step gradient** — each of the three working solutions is diluted from base 50% iodixanol (itself 5 parts OptiPrep : 1 part Diluent, since OptiPrep ships at 60% and $5/6 \times 60\% = 50\%$) with CitraHB, using $C_1V_1 = C_2V_2$:

$$V_{50\%\ needed} = V_{total} \times \frac{\%_{target}}{50\%} \qquad V_{CitraHB} = V_{total} - V_{50\%\ needed}$$

Per-sample totals: 15 mL of 50% (retained and dosed), 4 mL of 40%, 7.5 mL of 30%; all scale with $N_{samples} \times (1+overage)$. The undosed OptiPrep+Diluent base you actually make is larger than the 15 mL retained figure: $V_{base\ 50\%} = V_{50\%} + V_{50\%\ needed}^{(40\%)} + V_{50\%\ needed}^{(30\%)}$, since the 40%/30% pulls come out of that same base before it's dosed. Polyamine/DTT additives scale as $V_{total}/1000$; RNasin and Protector use the same $C_{final}/C_{stock} \times V_{total}$ formula.

<!-- TODO: RNasin/Protector in the retained 50% fraction are dosed at half the rate of the 40%/30% fractions (divided by 2). Preserved here as-is; confirm with JP whether this is intentional before scaling to large batches. -->
:::

### CitraHB Complete

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
chb_need    = chb_per_sample * scale
chb_vol     = Math.ceil(chb_need / 10) * 10
chb_tablets = chb_vol / 10

md`**Need ≈ ${fmt(chb_need)} mL for ${n_samples} sample(s) → make ${fmt(chb_vol, 0)} mL** (rounded up to a 10 mL multiple so protease tablets come out whole: **${chb_tablets} tablet(s)**)`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Protease inhibitor tablet",               "Per 10 mL": "1 whole tablet",                        "Total": `${chb_tablets} tablet(s)`},
  {Component: `RNasin (${rnasin_final} U/µL final)`,  "Per 10 mL": `${fmt(rnasin_vol(10000))} µL`,         "Total (µL)": fmt(rnasin_vol(chb_vol * 1000))},
  {Component: `Protector (${protector_final} U/µL final)`,      "Per 10 mL": `${fmt(protector_vol(10000))} µL`,           "Total (µL)": fmt(protector_vol(chb_vol * 1000))},
  {Component: "Spermidine (1000X)",                      "Per 10 mL": "10 µL",                                  "Total (µL)": fmt(chb_vol)},
  {Component: "Spermine (1000X)",                        "Per 10 mL": "10 µL",                                  "Total (µL)": fmt(chb_vol)},
  {Component: "Dithiothreitol (DTT, 1000X)",             "Per 10 mL": "10 µL",                                  "Total (µL)": fmt(chb_vol)},
  {Component: "CitraHB stock",                           "Per 10 mL": "to volume",                              "Total (mL)": fmt(chb_vol)}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

### Nuclei wash / resuspension buffer

::: {.callout-warning}
## No spermine, spermidine, or DTT in this buffer
These interfere with downstream cDNA synthesis. Make this buffer while the gradient is running.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
resus_per_sample = wash_per_spin * n_wash_spins + final_resus_uL / 1000
resus_vol   = resus_per_sample * scale
resus_bsa_g = resus_vol * 1 / 100

md`**${fmt(resus_per_sample)} mL/sample × ${n_samples} → ${fmt(resus_vol)} mL** (${n_wash_spins} wash spin(s) of ${fmt(wash_per_spin)} mL + ${fmt(final_resus_uL)} µL final resuspension)`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table([
  {Component: "Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA)",           "Amount": `${fmt(resus_bsa_g)} g (1% w/v)`},
  {Component: "1X Phosphate-Buffered Saline (PBS)",   "Amount": `to ${fmt(resus_vol)} mL`},
  {Component: `RNasin (${rnasin_final} U/µL final)`, "Amount": `${fmt(rnasin_vol(resus_vol))} mL`},
  {Component: `Protector (${protector_final} U/µL final)`,    "Amount": `${fmt(protector_vol(resus_vol))} mL`}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

### Iodixanol step gradient

::: {.callout-warning}
## Make base 50% first, split it, then add additives to each tube separately

The 40% and 30% solutions are diluted from **additive-free base 50% iodixanol**, not from the finished 50% solution in the first table below. Because some of that base gets pulled off before dosing, you make **more than the 15 mL/sample you'll end up dosing** — see the total below. Work in this order:

1. Make base 50% iodixanol with **OptiPrep + Diluent only**, at the larger "base 50% to make" total below. No spermidine, spermine, DTT, RNasin, or Protector yet.
2. Pull off the "50% iodixanol (above)" volumes listed in the 40% and 30% tables. That aliquot carries **no additives** with it.
3. You now have three separate tubes (leftover 50%, 40% mix, 30% mix). Add spermidine, spermine, DTT, RNasin, and Protector to **each tube**, scaled to that tube's own total volume.

Each tube is dosed once, on its own. The RNase inhibitor in the 40% and 30% tables is **not** a repeat of the 50%; the 50%-derived iodixanol in those tubes started out additive-free.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
v50 = 15  * scale   // retained & dosed with additives below — the "50% iodixanol" working solution
v40 = 4   * scale
v30 = 7.5 * scale

stock50_for_40 = v40 * 40/50
citrahb_40     = v40 - stock50_for_40

stock50_for_30 = v30 * 30/50
citrahb_30     = v30 - stock50_for_30

// Undosed OptiPrep+Diluent base has to cover v50 (retained, dosed below) PLUS what
// gets pulled off additive-free for the 40%/30% dilutions — make v50 alone and
// you come up stock50_for_40 + stock50_for_30 short after pulling.
base50_make = v50 + stock50_for_40 + stock50_for_30

optiprep_50 = base50_make * 5/6
diluent_50  = base50_make * 1/6

md`**Base 50% iodixanol to make: ${fmt(base50_make)} mL** (undosed — ${fmt(v50)} mL to retain and dose below, plus ${fmt(stock50_for_40)} mL + ${fmt(stock50_for_30)} mL to pull off additive-free for the 40%/30% dilutions)`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table([
  {Component: "OptiPrep",   "Volume (mL)": fmt(optiprep_50)},
  {Component: "Diluent",    "Volume (mL)": fmt(diluent_50)},
  {Component: "Spermidine (1000X)", "Volume (mL)": fmt(v50/1000)},
  {Component: "Spermine (1000X)",   "Volume (mL)": fmt(v50/1000)},
  {Component: "Dithiothreitol (DTT, 1000X)",        "Volume (mL)": fmt(v50/1000)},
  {Component: `RNasin (${rnasin_final} U/µL final)`, "Volume (mL)": fmt(rnasin_vol(v50) / 2)},
  {Component: `Protector (${protector_final} U/µL final)`,   "Volume (mL)": fmt(protector_vol(v50) / 2)}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`**40% iodixanol: ${fmt(v40)} mL total**`
```

```{ojs}
Inputs.table([

  {Component: "Dithiothreitol (DTT, 1000X)",           "Volume (mL)": fmt(v40/1000)},
```

```{ojs}
  {Component: "50% iodixanol (above)", "Volume (mL)": fmt(stock50_for_30)},
  {Component: "CitraHB",               "Volume (mL)": fmt(citrahb_30)},
  {Component: "Spermidine (1000X)",    "Volume (mL)": fmt(v30/1000)},
  {Component: "Spermine (1000X)",      "Volume (mL)": fmt(v30/1000)},
  {Component: "Dithiothreitol (DTT, 1000X)",           "Volume (mL)": fmt(v30/1000)},
  {Component: `RNasin (${rnasin_final} U/µL final)`, "Volume (mL)": fmt(rnasin_vol(v30))},
  {Component: `Protector (${protector_final} U/µL final)`,   "Volume (mL)": fmt(protector_vol(v30))}
], {layout: "auto"})
```

## Protocol

### Ice bucket map

Three buckets, organized by what's moving through the protocol rather than by reagent — keeps you from digging through "everything" mid-step.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
bucket = (title, items) => html`<div style="background:var(--bs-tertiary-bg, #f8f9fa);border:1px solid var(--bs-border-color, #dee2e6);border-radius:10px;padding:10px 12px;flex:1;min-width:180px;">
  <strong style="font-size:.85rem;">❄ ${title}</strong>
  <ul style="margin:6px 0 0;padding-left:18px;font-size:.82rem;color:var(--bs-secondary-color, #6c757d);">
    ${items.map(i => html`<li>${i}</li>`)}
  </ul>
</div>`

html`<div style="display:flex;gap:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:1rem;">
  ${bucket("Reagents", [
    "CitraHB Complete",
    "3 dosed iodixanol tubes (leftover 50%, 40%, 30%)",
    "Nuclei wash / resuspension buffer",
    "RNasin + Protector working aliquots",
    "1000X DTT / spermine / spermidine"
  ])}
  ${bucket("Active sample", [
    "Dounce homogenizer",
    "Chilled petri dish + tissue",
    "Detergent aliquot",
    "40 µm strainer",
    "This sample's filtrate tube"
  ])}
  ${bucket("Post-spin", [
    `Empty tubes for interface collection — label all ${n_samples} now`,
    "20 µm filters",
    "Spare wash buffer",
    "Trypan blue (0.2 µm filtered)"
  ])}
</div>`
```

### 1 · Tissue homogenization (~30 min)

::: {.callout-warning}
## No motorized homogenizer
Hand-dounce only; a rotor-stator or other motorized homogenizer shears nuclei and causes blebbing.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Under-homogenize on purpose
A run that was deliberately under-homogenized gave intact nuclei with **no blebbing at all**. Stop douncing as soon as nuclei start releasing; you do not need a clear homogenate, and over-douncing loses more nuclei than it frees.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Two-round dounce: a fixed bench-use split (Marissa's 4 mL + 1 mL, 256 + 64 µL),
// independent of the chb_per_sample "how much to make" toggle above — that toggle
// sets prep headroom, not what actually goes into the dounce.
round1_chb = 4
round2_chb = 1
round1_det = 256
round2_det = 64

md`Two-round dounce: the ≈ 5 mL CitraHB Complete used per sample is split ${fmt(round1_chb, 0)} mL + ${fmt(round2_chb, 0)} mL, and the 320 µL Detergent per sample is split ${fmt(round1_det, 0)} µL + ${fmt(round2_det, 0)} µL to match. (This is fixed bench usage — it doesn't change if you make extra CitraHB Complete above.)`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<div>${[
  checkStep("homog-a", "Pre-chill the 7 mL glass dounce homogenizer on ice."),
  checkStep("homog-b", "Cut snap-frozen tissue into < 0.5 cm pieces with clean scissors in a chilled petri dish on ice."),
  checkStep("homog-c", `Transfer the pieces to the dounce with ${fmt(round1_chb, 0)} mL CitraHB Complete; rest 7 min on ice.`),
  checkStep("homog-d", `Dounce ~20× with the loose pestle; add ${fmt(round1_det, 0)} µL Detergent; dounce ~20× with the tight pestle. Under-homogenize (see tip above); pull a drop to confirm nuclei are releasing.`),
  checkStep("homog-e", "Filter through a 40 µm strainer into a tube on ice; keep this filtrate."),
  checkStep("homog-f", `Return the tissue chunks left on top of the strainer to the dounce with the remaining ${fmt(round2_chb, 0)} mL CitraHB Complete + ${fmt(round2_det, 0)} µL Detergent; dounce again.`),
  checkStep("homog-g", `Filter through the same strainer and pool with the round-1 filtrate (≈ ${fmt(round1_chb + round2_chb, 0)} mL/sample).`)
]}</div>`
```

### 2 · Iodixanol gradient centrifugation (~1 hr + spin)

::: {.callout-warning}
## No brake on the spin
This spin is run on an **ultracentrifuge**: **18 min at 10,000×g at 4°C with no brake**. Braking disturbs the gradient interface and mixes the layers together, ruining nuclei recovery. Schedule the ultracentrifuge for **18 min** run time, but budget closer to **an hour** for the step overall; loading/vacuum draw-down, acceleration, and the unbraked coast to a stop add substantial time beyond the programmed 18 min.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<div>${[
  checkStep("grad-a", "Add 5 mL 50% iodixanol solution to the pooled homogenate filtrate and vortex to mix."),
  checkStep("grad-b", "Underlay the sample with 30% then 40% iodixanol solutions (per the gradient tables above)."),
  checkStep("grad-c", "Balance the conical tubes against each other on a scale, topping up the lighter tube(s) dropwise with cell culture grade water to within ~0.1 g; load balanced tubes opposite each other in the rotor."),
  checkStep("grad-d", "Centrifuge 18 min at 10,000×g, 4°C, no brake."),
  checkStep("grad-e", "Collect nuclei from the interface layer with a P1000 pipette; transfer to a new tube.")
]}</div>`
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Checklist
- [ ] Gradient tubes weighed against each other and balanced to within ~0.1 g before spinning
- [ ] Balanced tubes loaded opposite each other in the rotor
- [ ] Ultracentrifuge confirmed at no-brake setting
- [ ] Interface layer collected cleanly, minimal carryover of gradient layers
:::

### 3 · Nuclei wash & counting (~30 min)

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<div>${[
  checkStep("wash-1", "Collect nuclei from the gradient interface (Step 2e) into a 15 mL tube."),
  checkStep("wash-2", `Resuspend in ${fmt(wash_per_spin)} mL nuclei wash / resuspension buffer in a 15 mL tube; pipette gently, do not vortex.`),
  checkStep("wash-3", "Filter through a 20 µm filter."),
  checkStep("wash-4", `Spin 10 min at 500×g, 4°C; discard the supernatant.${n_wash_spins > 1 ? ` Repeat the resuspend (${fmt(wash_per_spin)} mL) + spin so the nuclei are washed ${n_wash_spins}× in total.` : ""}`),
  checkStep("wash-5", `Resuspend the final pellet in ${fmt(final_resus_uL)} µL; count on a hemocytometer (method below).`),
  checkStep("wash-6", "Load for single cell.")
]}</div>`
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Hemocytometer counting method
CitraPrep nuclei yields are typically too low for a reliable Countess (automated) read, so this is a **manual hemocytometer count** every time; do not substitute the Countess.

a. Filter your trypan blue stock through a 0.2 µm filter before use; unfiltered trypan blue carries particulates that get miscounted as nuclei, and this matters more at low nuclei numbers where a few false counts skew the result.
b. Mix the nuclei suspension with filtered trypan blue at a **1:1** ratio (e.g. 10 µL suspension + 10 µL trypan blue, dilution factor = 2).
c. Load 10 µL of the mix onto the hemocytometer; let it wick in by capillary action, no bubbles.
d. Under the microscope, count nuclei in the 4 corner grid squares (16 small squares each). Use the standard hemocytometer counting rule: count nuclei touching the top and left borders of a square, but not the bottom or right, to avoid double-counting nuclei that sit on a line.
e. Calculate concentration:

$$Nuclei/mL = \frac{\text{sum of nuclei in 4 corner squares}}{4} \times 2\ (\text{dilution factor}) \times 10^4$$

Divide by 1000 to convert to nuclei/µL for loading calculations.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Checklist
- [ ] Trypan blue filtered (0.2 µm) before use
- [ ] Nuclei suspension diluted 1:1 with trypan blue
- [ ] Nuclei intact and free of debris under the hemocytometer
- [ ] Nuclei concentration: _______ nuclei/µL
- [ ] Loaded for single-cell run at: _______
:::
